title: Privacy‑first ingest middleware with schema version negotiation
creator: Arielle Chen
body:
Summary:
Implement a privacy‑first, tenant‑aware ingest middleware that performs structured-log schema version negotiation, deterministic sampling, and PII-safe transformations before forwarding to Loki/ELK or long‑term S3. This middleware sits between edge forwarders (Vector/Fluent Bit) and our aggregation plane and is intended to replace multiple ad‑hoc enrichers currently deployed in front of Loki.

Goals:
- Ensure no raw PII leaves the ingest boundary for flagged tenants (configurable per-tenant rules).
- Support schema version negotiation so producers can include a schema_version field and we can apply the correct normalization/transforms server-side.
- Propagate or synthesize correlation IDs and hashed trace identifiers for safe joins across systems without exposing raw trace ids.
- Provide deterministic sampling & tenant rate-limits with observable counters and per-tenant backpressure signals.
- Emit standardized metrics (ingest.rps, ingest.latency_ms_p95, redact.count, sample.rate_by_tenant) and dashboards for SLO/regression detection.

Non-goals:
- Full replacement of the existing long-term archive pipeline (S3 export remains separate).
- Deep schema migration tooling for producers — we provide server-side adapters to smooth rollouts.

Technical approach:
1) Edge expectations: producers send JSON structured logs with minimal envelope: {"ts","tenant_id","schema_version","payload","trace_id?","correlation_id?"}. Edge forwarders will append host/service metadata.
2) Middleware binary: Rust service (for memory/safety/perf) with a pluggable pipeline: proto‑parser -> schema adapter -> PII redactor -> sampling/throttle -> enrich (kv cache lookup) -> output router.
3) Schema adapters: small WASM or Rust modules selected by schema_version; adapters transform payload to canonical v1 internal shape. Adapters stored in GCS and hot‑reloaded.
4) PII redaction: rules engine per tenant. Redaction modes: drop, hash (sha256 with tenant salt), mask. Hashing used for trace_id when trace privacy is enabled. Configurable global allowlist for certain attributes (e.g., service.name).
5) Correlation handling: if correlation_id present, preserve; if only trace_id present and privacy flag enabled, replace with trace_hash = SHA256(tenant_salt + trace_id) and emit trace_hash in meta as trace_fingerprint. Original trace_id is not logged.
6) Deterministic sampling: hashing on (tenant_id + trace_fingerprint) with configurable sample rates per tenant and route (errors always sampled).
7) Output: route to Loki for short-term query indexes (labels set from canonical fields), mirrored routed events to ELK for text search for selected tenants, and batched S3 for retention. Backpressure via HTTP 429 to forwarders and a metrics socket for Vector to inspect.

Acceptance criteria:
- Middleware accepts expected envelope and normalizes 99% of incoming schema variants from current producers in staging.
- Verified PII redaction for 3 test tenants (drop, hash, mask) with automated unit/integration tests.
- Deterministic sampling reproduces sample selection across restarts for a given tenant+trace.
- End-to-end latency (edge -> middleware -> loki) p95 under 350ms at 500 rps sustained in perf tests.
- Dashboards created: 'Ingest Overview', 'Per-tenant Redaction & Sampling', 'Ingest Backpressure & Throttles'.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (dev/stage): implement adapters and rule engine; run in shadow mode for 2 weeks, compare outputs with current pipeline.
- Phase 1 (canary): route 5% of production traffic (non-critical tenants) through middleware; enable reject/backpressure only on backends if overload detected.
- Phase 2 (gradual enable): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks with monitoring alerts for increased error rate or query regressions.
- Rollback: toggle per-tenant routing; preserve raw backup stream to S3 for 48 hours to allow reindexing.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for adapters and redaction rules.
- Integration tests: staged producers emit known PII and schema variants; assert no raw secrets forwarded.
- Perf tests in perf cluster using real-ish payload mixes (50/30/20 small/medium/large).
- Chaos: simulate hot‑reload of adapters, and network partitions to ensure deterministic sampling persistence.

Observability & dashboards:
- New metrics emitted via Prometheus metrics endpoint: ingest.requests_total, ingest.rejected_total, ingest.redactions_total, ingest.sampled_total, ingest.latency_seconds_bucket.
- Traces instrumented with OpenTelemetry inside the middleware; spans emit sanitized attributes only.
- Dashboards: team will author Grafana panels under 'Ingest - Privacy Middleware'. Alerts: high reject rate >0.5% sustained, p95 latency >500ms, redactions spike indicating misconfiguration.

Security & compliance notes:
- security_review_required: true — coordinate with Security for tenant salt KMS storage and adapter signing.
- Adapter artifacts must be signed; middleware verifies signatures before hot‑reload.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should we support per-field regex-based redaction authored by tenants or only curated server-side rules? (Security prefers curated rules)
- How long to keep raw backup in S3 by default? (30 days vs 48 hours — propose 48 hours to reduce exposure)
- Do we allow tenant-side provided salt for hashing? (security risk; prefer server-managed salts)

Risks:
- Misconfigured redaction rules could cause PII leakage — mitigated by test suite and staging shadowing.
- Performance overhead of adapters/hot-reload — we will benchmark and consider JITing common adapters.

Deliverables / artifacts:
- RFC doc (Confluence): link below.
- Prototype binary + adapter examples in repo: link below.
- Grafana dashboards and alert rules: link below.

Next steps (short term):
- Complete prototypes for redaction rules and schema adapters (assigned).
- Security sync for KMS & adapter signing.
- Perf run and iterate on memory pools and batching knobs.

2025-02-25: Security requested adapter signing and KMS-managed tenant salts. Raised to security for review. - Diego
2025-03-02: Perf test (500 rps) completed in perf cluster; p95 latency 320ms with modest memory tuning. Need one more tuning pass on batch flush. - Diego
2025-03-04: QA found an edge case where nested email fields were not caught by current redaction rules; added new test case and adapter patch. - Arielle
